title: Agents & Tool Use
blurb: From prompting tricks to systems that act. The through-line is giving a model a scratchpad, then a tool, then a loop.

anchors.note: Ask for the reasoning and accuracy jumps on multi-step problems. The prompt as a scratchpad.
Sample several reasoning paths and take the majority. Cheap, and reliably better than one greedy chain.
Interleaves reasoning with actions so the model can look things up mid-thought. The template most agents still follow.
The model teaches itself when to call an API, in a self-supervised way. Tool use as a learned skill.
Verbal self-critique carried across attempts, as an alternative to weight updates.
Search over a tree of partial reasoning states rather than committing to one chain.
Memory, reflection and planning in a simulated society. Where the agent-architecture vocabulary comes from.
An open-ended agent that writes and stores its own skills. Lifelong learning without gradient updates.
